review_notes:
I read all of Finite.lean. I also read the shared API in TauCeti/Topology/Covering/Category.lean, covering CoveringSpace.FullSubcategory, its mk, mk_coe, mk_proj, forget_obj_mk and forget, and Over.isCoveringMap_iff. I grepped for uses of hasFiniteFibers across the repo.

The simp set here is small:
- Over.hasFiniteFibers_iff is a simp lemma proved by Iff.rfl. It follows the same pattern as the existing Over.isCoveringMap_iff. Its right-hand side has no cycle.
- mk_coe, mk_proj and forget_obj_mk are all rfl lemmas. They are stated for the local mk, which is an @[expose] def. The general CoveringSpace.FullSubcategory.mk_coe and mk_proj therefore do not compete with them. The docstring in Category.lean explains why they are restated.
- finite_fiber is an instance whose statement uses p.proj, which is an abbrev. I saw no conflict with the simp lemmas.

I considered whether Set.finite_coe_iff competes with the Finite ↥(...) forms. It is not a simp lemma in this Mathlib (Mathlib/Basic/Finite/Defs.lean, `theorem finite_coe_iff {s : Set α} : Finite s ↔ s.Finite := .rfl`), so there is no competing normal form.

Remaining uncertainty: I cannot run Lean, so I did not check how simp actually behaves. I also did not look at downstream simp calls outside this repo's uses of hasFiniteFibers, which are the term-mode uses in this file and one use in GaloisCategory.lean.
